1:   Krishna.
2:   Therefore, who doeth work rightful to do,
3:   Not seeking gain from work, that man, O Prince!
4:   Is Sanyasi and Yogi--both in one
5:   And he is neither who lights not the flame
6:   Of sacrifice, nor setteth hand to task.
7: 
8:   Regard as true Renouncer him that makes
9:   Worship by work, for who renounceth not
10:   Works not as Yogin. So is that well said:
11:   "By works the votary doth rise to faith,
12:   And saintship is the ceasing from all works;
13:   Because the perfect Yogin acts--but acts
14:   Unmoved by passions and unbound by deeds,
15:   Setting result aside.
16: 
17:   Let each man raise
18:   The Self by Soul, not trample down his Self,
19:   Since Soul that is Self's friend may grow Self's foe.
20:   Soul is Self's friend when Self doth rule o'er Self,
21:   But Self turns enemy if Soul's own self
22:   Hates Self as not itself.[FN#10]
23: 
24:   The sovereign soul
25:   Of him who lives self-governed and at peace
26:   Is centred in itself, taking alike
27:   Pleasure and pain; heat, cold; glory and shame.
28:   He is the Yogi, he is Yukta, glad
29:   With joy of light and truth; dwelling apart
30:   Upon a peak, with senses subjugate
31:   Whereto the clod, the rock, the glistering gold
32:   Show all as one. By this sign is he known
33:   Being of equal grace to comrades, friends,
34:   Chance-comers, strangers, lovers, enemies,
35:   Aliens and kinsmen; loving all alike,
36:   Evil or good.
37: 
38:   Sequestered should he sit,
39:   Steadfastly meditating, solitary,
40:   His thoughts controlled, his passions laid away,
41:   Quit of belongings. In a fair, still spot
42:   Having his fixed abode,--not too much raised,
43:   Nor yet too low,--let him abide, his goods
44:   A cloth, a deerskin, and the Kusa-grass.
45:   There, setting hard his mind upon The One,
46:   Restraining heart and senses, silent, calm,
47:   Let him accomplish Yoga, and achieve
48:   Pureness of soul, holding immovable
49:   Body and neck and head, his gaze absorbed
50:   Upon his nose-end,[FN#11] rapt from all around,
51:   Tranquil in spirit, free of fear, intent
52:   Upon his Brahmacharya vow, devout,
53:   Musing on Me, lost in the thought of Me.
54:   That Yojin, so devoted, so controlled,
55:   Comes to the peace beyond,--My peace, the peace
56:   Of high Nirvana!
57: 
58:   But for earthly needs
59:   Religion is not his who too much fasts
60:   Or too much feasts, nor his who sleeps away
61:   An idle mind; nor his who wears to waste
62:   His strength in vigils. Nay, Arjuna! call
63:   That the true piety which most removes
64:   Earth-aches and ills, where one is moderate
65:   In eating and in resting, and in sport;
66:   Measured in wish and act; sleeping betimes,
67:   Waking betimes for duty.
68: 
69:   When the man,
70:   So living, centres on his soul the thought
71:   Straitly restrained--untouched internally
72:   By stress of sense--then is he Yukta. See!
73:   Steadfast a lamp burns sheltered from the wind;
74:   Such is the likeness of the Yogi's mind
75:   Shut from sense-storms and burning bright to Heaven.
76:   When mind broods placid, soothed with holy wont;
77:   When Self contemplates self, and in itself
78:   Hath comfort; when it knows the nameless joy
79:   Beyond all scope of sense, revealed to soul--
80:   Only to soul! and, knowing, wavers not,
81:   True to the farther Truth; when, holding this,
82:   It deems no other treasure comparable,
83:   But, harboured there, cannot be stirred or shook
84:   By any gravest grief, call that state "peace,"
85:   That happy severance Yoga; call that man
86:   The perfect Yogin!
87: 
88:   Steadfastly the will
89:   Must toil thereto, till efforts end in ease,
90:   And thought has passed from thinking. Shaking off
91:   All longings bred by dreams of fame and gain,
92:   Shutting the doorways of the senses close
93:   With watchful ward; so, step by step, it comes
94:   To gift of peace assured and heart assuaged,
95:   When the mind dwells self-wrapped, and the soul broods
96:   Cumberless. But, as often as the heart
97:   Breaks--wild and wavering--from control, so oft
98:   Let him re-curb it, let him rein it back
99:   To the soul's governance; for perfect bliss
100:   Grows only in the bosom tranquillised,
101:   The spirit passionless, purged from offence,
102:   Vowed to the Infinite. He who thus vows
103:   His soul to the Supreme Soul, quitting sin,
104:   Passes unhindered to the endless bliss
105:   Of unity with Brahma. He so vowed,
106:   So blended, sees the Life-Soul resident
107:   In all things living, and all living things
108:   In that Life-Soul contained. And whoso thus
109:   Discerneth Me in all, and all in Me,
110:   I never let him go; nor looseneth he
111:   Hold upon Me; but, dwell he where he may,
112:   Whate'er his life, in Me he dwells and lives,
113:   Because he knows and worships Me, Who dwell
114:   In all which lives, and cleaves to Me in all.
115:   Arjuna! if a man sees everywhere--
116:   Taught by his own similitude--one Life,
117:   One Essence in the Evil and the Good,
118:   Hold him a Yogi, yea! well-perfected!
119: 
120:   Arjuna.
121:   Slayer of Madhu! yet again, this Yog,
122:   This Peace, derived from equanimity,
123:   Made known by thee--I see no fixity
124:   Therein, no rest, because the heart of men
125:   Is unfixed, Krishna! rash, tumultuous,
126:   Wilful and strong. It were all one, I think,
127:   To hold the wayward wind, as tame man's heart.
128: 
129:   Krishna.
130:   Hero long-armed! beyond denial, hard
131:   Man's heart is to restrain, and wavering;
132:   Yet may it grow restrained by habit, Prince!
133:   By wont of self-command. This Yog, I say,
134:   Cometh not lightly to th' ungoverned ones;
135:   But he who will be master of himself
136:   Shall win it, if he stoutly strive thereto.
137: 
138:   Arjuna.
139:   And what road goeth he who, having faith,
140:   Fails, Krishna! in the striving; falling back
141:   From holiness, missing the perfect rule?
142:   Is he not lost, straying from Brahma's light,
143:   Like the vain cloud, which floats 'twixt earth and heaven
144:   When lightning splits it, and it vanisheth?
145:   Fain would I hear thee answer me herein,
146:   Since, Krishna! none save thou can clear the doubt.
147: 
148:   Krishna.
149:   He is not lost, thou Son of Pritha! No!
150:   Nor earth, nor heaven is forfeit, even for him,
151:   Because no heart that holds one right desire
152:   Treadeth the road of loss! He who should fail,
153:   Desiring righteousness, cometh at death
154:   Unto the Region of the Just; dwells there
155:   Measureless years, and being born anew,
156:   Beginneth life again in some fair home
157:   Amid the mild and happy. It may chance
158:   He doth descend into a Yogin house
159:   On Virtue's breast; but that is rare! Such birth
160:   Is hard to be obtained on this earth, Chief!
161:   So hath he back again what heights of heart
162:   He did achieve, and so he strives anew
163:   To perfectness, with better hope, dear Prince!
164:   For by the old desire he is drawn on
165:   Unwittingly; and only to desire
166:   The purity of Yog is to pass
167:   Beyond the Sabdabrahm, the spoken Ved.
168:   But, being Yogi, striving strong and long,
169:   Purged from transgressions, perfected by births
170:   Following on births, he plants his feet at last
171:   Upon the farther path. Such as one ranks
172:   Above ascetics, higher than the wise,
173:   Beyond achievers of vast deeds! Be thou
174:   Yogi Arjuna! And of such believe,
175:   Truest and best is he who worships Me
176:   With inmost soul, stayed on My Mystery!
177: 
178:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER VI. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
179:   Entitled "Atmasanyamayog,"
180:   Or "The Book of Religion by Self-Restraint."

Krishna.
  Therefore, who doeth work rightful to do,
  Not seeking gain from work, that man, O Prince!
  Is Sanyasi and Yogi--both in one
  And he is neither who lights not the flame

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.1 The Blessed Lord said He who performs his bounden duty without depending on the fruits of his actions he is a Sannyasi and a Yogi; not he who is without fire and without action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.1 "Lord Shri Krishna said: He who acts because it is his duty, not thinking of the consequences, is really spiritual and a true ascetic; and not he who merely observes rituals or who shuns all action.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.1 The Blessed Lord said He who performs an action which is his duty, without depending on the result of action, he is a monk and a yogi; (but) not (so in) he who does not keep a fire and is actionless.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.2 Do thou, O Arjuna, know Yoga to be that which they call renunciation; no one verily becomes a Yogi who has not renounced thoughts.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.2 O Arjuna! Renunciation is in fact what is called Right Action. No one can become spiritual who has not renounced all desire.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.2 That which they call monasticism, know that to be Yoa, O Pandava, For, nobody who has not given up expectations can be a yogi.

witnesses.text: 6.3 For a sage who wishes to attain to Yoga, action is said to be the means; for the same sage who has attained to Yoga, inaction (iescence) is said to be the means.

witnesses.text: 6.3 For the sage who seeks the heights of spiritual meditation, practice is the only method, and when he has attained them, he must maintain himself there by continual self-control.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.3 For the sage who wishes to ascend to (Dhyana-) yoga, action is said to be the means. For that person, when he has ascended to (Dhyana-)yoga, inaction alone is said to be the means.

arnold.content:
Because the perfect Yogin acts--but acts

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.4 When a man is not attached to the sense-objects or to actions, having renounced all thoughts, then he is said to have attained to Yoga.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.4 When a man renounces even the thought of initiating action, when he is not interested in sense objects or any results which may flow from his acts, then in truth he understands spirituality.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.4 Verily, [Verily: This word emphasizes the fact that, since attachment to sense objects like sound etc. and to actions is an obstacle in the path of Yoga, therefore the removal of that obstruction is the means to its attainment.] when a man who has given up thought about everything does not get attached to sense-objects or acitons, he is then said to be established in Yoga.

witnesses.text: 6.5 One should raise oneself by one's Self alone; let not one lower oneself; for the Self alone is the friend of oneself, and the Self alone is the enemy of oneself.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.6 Of him, by whom has been conered his very self by the self, his self is the friend of his self. But, for one who has not conered his self, his self itself acts inimically like an enemy.

  Pureness of soul,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.12 There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and the senses controlled, let him, seated on the seat, practise Yoga for the purification of the self.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.12 Seated thus, his mind concentrated, its functions controlled and his senses governed, let him practise meditation for the purification of his lower nature.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.12 (and) sitting on that seat, he should concentrate his mind for the purification of the internal organ, making the mind one-pointed and keeping the actions of the mind and senses under control.

records.sanskrit:
समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः।
सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥
records.iast:
samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ
samprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
holding immovable
  Body and neck and head, his gaze absorbed
  Upon his nose-end,[FN#11] rapt from all around,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.13 Let him firmly hold his body, head and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of his nose, without looking around.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.13 Let him hold body, head and neck erect, motionless and steady; let him look fixedly at the tip of his nose, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.13 Holding the body, head and neck erect and still, being steady, looking at the tip of his own nose-and not looking around;

records.sanskrit:
प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः।
मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥
records.iast:
praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ
manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Tranquil in spirit, free of fear, intent
  Upon his Brahmacharya vow, devout,
  Musing on Me, lost in the thought of Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.14 Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of a Brahmachari, having controlled the mind, thinking of Me and balanced in mind, let him sit, having Me as his supreme goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.14 With peace in his heart and nor fear, observing the vow of celibacy, with mind controlled and fixed on Me, let the student lose himself in contemplation of Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.14 He should remain seated with a placid mind, free from fear, firm in the vow of a celibate, and with the mind fixed on Me by controlling it through concentration, having Me as the supreme Goal.

records.sanskrit:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः।
शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥
records.iast:
yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ
śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthāmadhigacchati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
That Yojin, so devoted, so controlled,
  Comes to the peace beyond,--My peace, the peace
  Of high Nirvana!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.15 Thus always keeping the mind balanced, the Yogi, with the mind controlled, attains to the peace abiding in Me, which culminates in liberation.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.15 Thus keeping his mind always in communion with Me, and with his thoughts subdued, he shall attain that Peace which is mine and which will lead him to liberation at last.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.15 Concentrating the mind thus for ever, the yogi of controlled mind achieves the Peace which culminates in Liberation and which abides in Me.

records.sanskrit:
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः।
न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
records.iast:
nātyaśnatastu yogo.asti na caikāntamanaśnataḥ
na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But for earthly needs
  Religion is not his who too much fasts
  Or too much feasts, nor his who sleeps away
  An idle mind; nor his who wears to waste
  His strength in vigils.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.16 Verily Yoga is not possible for him who eats too much, nor for him who does not eat at all, nor for him who sleeps too much, nor for him who is (always) awake, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.16 Meditation is not for him who eats too much, not for him who eats not at all; not for him who is overmuch addicted to sleep, not for him who is always awake.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.16 But, O Arjuna, Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; neither for one who habitually sleeps too long, nor surely for one who keeps awake.

records.sanskrit:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
records.iast:
yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu
yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Nay, Arjuna! call
  That the true piety which most removes
  Earth-aches and ills, where one is moderate
  In eating and in resting, and in sport;
  Measured in wish and act; sleeping betimes,
  Waking betimes for duty.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
6.17 Yoga becomes the destroyer of pain for him who is moderate in eating and recreation (such
as walking, etc.), who is moderate in exertion in actions, who is moderate in sleep and wakefulness.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.17 But for him who regulates his food and recreation, who is balanced in action, in sleep and in waking, it shall dispel all unhappiness.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.17 Yoga becomes a destroyer of sorrow of one whose eating and movements are regulated, whose effort in works is moderate, and whose sleep and wakefulness are temperate.

records.sanskrit:
यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते।
निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥
records.iast:
yadā viniyataṃ cittamātmanyevāvatiṣṭhate
niḥspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ityucyate tadā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
When the man,
  So living, centres on his soul the thought
  Straitly restrained--untouched internally
  By stress of sense--then is he Yukta.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.18 When the perfectly controlled mind rests in the Self only, free from longing for all the objects of desires, then it is said, 'He is united'.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.18 When the mind, completely controlled, is centered in the Self, and free from all earthly desires, then is the man truly spiritual.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.18 A man who has become free from hankering for all desirable objects is then said to be Self-absorbed when the controlled mind rests in the Self alone.

records.sanskrit:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
records.iast:
yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā
yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
See!
  Steadfast a lamp burns sheltered from the wind;
  Such is the likeness of the Yogi's mind
  Shut from sense-storms and burning bright to Heaven.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.19 As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker to such is compared the Yogi of controlled mind, practising Yoga in the Self (or absorbed in the Yoga of the Self).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.19 The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is as a lamp which does not flicker, since it stands sheltered from every wind.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.19 As a lamp kept in a windless place does not flicker, such is the simile thought of for the yogi whose mind is under control, and who is engaged in concentration on the Self.

records.sanskrit:
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया।
यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥
records.iast:
yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevayā
yatra caivātmanātmānaṃ paśyannātmani tuṣyati
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.20 When the mind, restrained by the practice of Yoga attains to quietude and when seeing the Self by the self, he is satisfied in his own Self.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.20 There, where the whole nature is seen in the light of the Self, where the man abides within his Self and is satisfied there, its functions restrained by its union with the Divine, the mind finds rest.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.20 At the time when the mind restrained through the practice of Yoga gets withdrawn, and just when by seeing the Self by the self one remains contented in the Self alone [A.G. construes the word eva (certainly) with tusyati (remains contented).-Tr.];

records.sanskrit:
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद् बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम्।
वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥
records.iast:
sukhamātyantikaṃ yattad buddhigrāhyamatīndriyam
vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
when it knows the nameless joy
  Beyond all scope of sense, revealed to soul--
  Only to soul! and, knowing, wavers not,
  True to the farther Truth;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.21 When he (the Yogi) feels that Infinite Bliss which can be grasped by the (pure) intellect and which transcends the senses, and established wherein he never moves from the Reality.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.21 When he enjoys the Bliss which passes sense, and which only the Pure Intellect can grasp, when he comes to rest within his own highest Self, never again will he stray from reality.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.21 When one experienece that absolute Blisss which can be intuited by the intellect and which is beyond the senses, and being established (thus) this person surely does not swerve from Reality;

records.sanskrit:
यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः।
यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥
records.iast:
yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ
yasminsthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
when, holding this,
  It deems no other treasure comparable,
  But, harboured there, cannot be stirred or shook
  By any gravest grief,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.22 Which, having obtained, he thinks there is no other gain superior to it; wherein estabished, he is not moved even by heavy sorrow.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.22 Finding That, he will realise that there is no possession so precious. And when once established here, no calamity can disturb him.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.22 Obtaining which one does not think of any other acisition to be superior to that, and being established in which one is not perturbed even by great sorrow;

records.sanskrit:
तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम्।
स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥
records.iast:
taṃ vidyād duḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam
sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo.anirviṇṇacetasā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
call that state "peace,"
  That happy severance Yoga; call that man
  The perfect Yogin!

  Steadfastly the will
  Must toil thereto, till efforts end in ease,
  And thought has passed from thinking.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.23 Let that be known by the name of Yoga, the severance from union with pain. This Yoga should be practised with determination and with an undesponding mind.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.23 This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality. It should be practised with determination and with a heart which refuses to be depressed.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.23 One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga has to be practised with perservance and with an undepressed heart.

records.sanskrit:
सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः।
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥
records.iast:
saṅkalpaprabhavānkāmāṃstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ
manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Shaking off
  All longings bred by dreams of fame and gain,
  Shutting the doorways of the senses close
  With watchful ward;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.24 Abandoning without reserve all desires born of Sankalpa (thought and imagination) and completely restraining the whole group of the senses by the mind from all sides.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.24 Renouncing every desire which imagination can conceive, controlling the senses at every point by the power of mind;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.24 By totally eschewing all desires which arise from thoughts, and restraining with the mind itself all the organs from every side;

records.sanskrit:
शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया।
आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
records.iast:
śanaiḥ śanairuparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā
ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
so, step by step, it comes
  To gift of peace assured and heart assuaged,
  When the mind dwells self-wrapped, and the soul broods
  Cumberless.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.25 Little by little let him attain to ietude by the intellect held firmly; having made the mind establish itself in the Self, let him not think of anything.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.25 Little by little, by the help of his reason controlled by fortitude, let him attain peace; and, fixing his mind on the Self, let him not think of any other thing.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.25 One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

records.sanskrit:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
records.iast:
yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram
tatastato niyamyaitadātmanyeva vaśaṃ nayet
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But, as often as the heart
  Breaks--wild and wavering--from control, so oft
  Let him re-curb it, let him rein it back
  To the soul's governance;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.26 From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, from that let him restrain it and bring it under the control of the Self alone.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.26 When the volatile and wavering mind would wander, let him restrain it and bring it again to its allegiance to the Self.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.26 (The yogi) should bring (this mind) under the subjugation of the Self Itself, by restraining it from all those causes whatever due to which the restless, unsteady mind wanders away.

records.sanskrit:
प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम्।
उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥
records.iast:
praśāntamanasaṃ hyenaṃ yoginaṃ sukhamuttamam
upaiti śāntarajasaṃ brahmabhūtamakalmaṣam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
for perfect bliss
  Grows only in the bosom tranquillised,
  The spirit passionless, purged from offence,
  Vowed to the Infinite.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.27 Supreme Bliss verily comes to this Yogi whose mind is ite peaceful, whose passion is ieted, who has become Brahman and who is free from sin.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.27 Supreme Bliss is the lot of the sage, whose mind attains Peace, whose passions subside, who is without sin, and who becomes one with the Absolute.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.27 Supreme Bliss comes to this yogi alone whose mind has become perfectly tranil, whose (ality of) rajas has been eliminated, who has become identified with Brahman, and is taintless.

records.sanskrit:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः।
सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥
records.iast:
yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī vigatakalmaṣaḥ
sukhena brahmasaṃsparśamatyantaṃ sukhamaśnute
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He who thus vows
  His soul to the Supreme Soul, quitting sin,
  Passes unhindered to the endless bliss
  Of unity with Brahma.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.28 The Yogi, always engaging the mind thus (in the practice of Yoga), freed from sins, easily enjoys the Infinite Bliss of contact with Brahman (the Eternal).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.28 Thus, free from sin, abiding always in the Eternal, the saint enjoys without effort the Bliss which flows from realisation of the Infinite.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.28 By concentrating his mind constantly thus, the taintless yogi easily attains the absolute Bliss of contact with Brahman.

records.sanskrit:
सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि।
ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
records.iast:
sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani
īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He so vowed,
  So blended, sees the Life-Soul resident
  In all things living, and all living things
  In that Life-Soul contained.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.29 With the mind harmonised by Yoga he sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self; he sees the same everywhere.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.29 He who experiences the unity of life sees his own Self in all beings, and all beings in his own Self, and looks on everything with an impartial eye;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.29 One who has his mind Self-absorbed through Yoga, and who has the vision of sameness every-where, see this Self existing in everything, and every-thing in his Self.

records.sanskrit:
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
records.iast:
yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And whoso thus
  Discerneth Me in all, and all in Me,
  I never let him go; nor looseneth he
  Hold upon Me;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.30 He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, he never becomes separated from Me, nor do I become separated from him.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.30 He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, him shall I never forsake, nor shall he lose Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.30 One who sees Me in everything, and sees all things in Me-I do not out of his vision, and he also is not lost to My vision.

records.sanskrit:
सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥
records.iast:
sarvabhūtasthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajatyekatvamāsthitaḥ
sarvathā vartamāno.api sa yogī mayi vartate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
but, dwell he where he may,
  Whate'er his life, in Me he dwells and lives,
  Because he knows and worships Me, Who dwell
  In all which lives, and cleaves to Me in all.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.31 He who, being established in unity, worships Me Who dwells in all beings, that Yogi abides in Me, whatever may be his mode of living.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.31 The sage who realises the unity of life and who worships Me in all beings, lives in Me, whatever may be his lot.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.31 That yogi who, being established in unity, adores Me as existing in all things, he exist in Me-in whatever condition he may be.

records.sanskrit:
आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन।
सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥
records.iast:
ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo.arjuna
sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ sa yogī paramo mataḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Arjuna! if a man sees everywhere--
  Taught by his own similitude--one Life,
  One Essence in the Evil and the Good,
  Hold him a Yogi, yea! well-perfected!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.32 He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, sees eality everywhere, be it pleasure or pain, he is regarded as the highest Yogi.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.32 O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.32 O Arjuna, that yogi is considered the best who judges what is happiness and sorrow in all beings by the same standard as he would apply to himself.

records.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन।
एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
records.iast:
arjuna uvāca
yo.ayaṃ yogastvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana
etasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi cañcalatvātsthitiṃ sthirām
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  Slayer of Madhu! yet again, this Yog,
  This Peace, derived from equanimity,
  Made known by thee--I see no fixity
  Therein, no rest,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.33 Arjuna said This Yoga of eanimity taught by Thee, O Krishna, I do not see its steady continuance, because of the restlessness (of the mind).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.33 Arjuna said: I do not see how I can attain this state of equanimity which Thou has revealed, owing to the restlessness of my mind.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.33 Arjuna said O Madhusudana (Krsna), this Yoga that has been spoken of by You as sameness, I do not see its steady continuance, owing to the restlessness (of the mind).

records.sanskrit:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद् दृढम्।
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
records.iast:
cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham
tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye vāyoriva suduṣkaram
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
because the heart of men
  Is unfixed, Krishna! rash, tumultuous,
  Wilful and strong. It were all one, I think,
  To hold the wayward wind, as tame man's heart.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.34 The mind verily is restless, turbulent, strong and unyielding, O Krishna: I deem it as difficult to control it as to control the wind.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.34 My Lord! Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate and strong, yea extremely difficult as the wind to control.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.34 For, O Krsna, the mind is unsteady, turbulent, strong and obstinate. I consider its control to be as greatly difficult as of the wind.

records.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम्।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
records.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calam
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  Hero long-armed! beyond denial, hard
  Man's heart is to restrain, and wavering;
  Yet may it grow restrained by habit, Prince!
  By wont of self-command.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.35 The Blessed Lord said Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the mind is difficult to control and restless; but by practice and by dispassion it may be restrained.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.35 Lord Shri Krishna replied: Doubtless, O Mighty One, the mind is fickle and exceedingly difficult to restrain, but, O Son of Kunti, with practice and renunciation it can be done.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.35 The Blessed Lord said O mighty-armed one, undoubtedly the mind is untractable and restless. But, O son of Kunti, it is brought under control through practice and detachment.

records.sanskrit:
असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः।
वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥
records.iast:
asaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ
vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo.avāptumupāyataḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
This Yog, I say,
  Cometh not lightly to th' ungoverned ones;
  But he who will be master of himself
  Shall win it, if he stoutly strive thereto.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.36 I think Yoga is hard to be attained by one of uncontrolled self, but the self-controlled and striving one can attain to it by the (proper) means.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.36 It is not possible to attain Self-Realisation if a man does not know how to control himself; but for him who, striving by proper means, learns such control, it is possible.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.36 My conviction is that Yoga is difficult to be attained by one of uncontrolled mind. But it is possible to be attained through the (above) means by one who strives and has a controlled mind.

records.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः।
अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
records.iast:
arjuna uvāca
ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāccalitamānasaḥ
aprāpya yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  And what road goeth he who, having faith,
  Fails, Krishna! in the striving; falling back
  From holiness, missing the perfect rule?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.37 Arjuna said He who is unable to control himself though he has the faith, and whose mind wanders away from Yoga, what end does he, having failed to attain perfection in Yoga, mee,t O Krishna?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.37 Arjuna asked: He who fails to control himself, whose mind falls from spiritual contemplation, who attains not perfection but retains his faith, what of him, my Lord?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.37 Arjuna said O krsna, failing to achieve perfection in Yoga, what goal does one attain who, though possessed of faith, is not diligent and whose mind becomes deflected from Yoga?

records.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति।
अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
records.iast:
kaccinnobhayavibhraṣṭaśchinnābhramiva naśyati
apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Is he not lost, straying from Brahma's light,
  Like the vain cloud, which floats 'twixt earth and heaven
  When lightning splits it, and it vanisheth?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: Shri Purohit Swami did not comment on this sloka

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: Swami Gambirananda did not comment on this sloka

records.sanskrit:
एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः।
त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
records.iast:
etanme saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇa chettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ
tvadanyaḥ saṃśayasyāsya chettā na hyupapadyate
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Fain would I hear thee answer me herein,
  Since, Krishna! none save thou can clear the doubt.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.39 This doubt of mine, O Krishna, do Thou dispel completely; because it is not possible for any but Thee to dispel this doubt.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.39 My Lord! Thou art worthy to solve this doubt once and for all; save Thyself there is no one competent to do so.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.39 O Krsna, You should totally eradicate this doubt of mine. For, none other than Yourself can be the dispeller of this doubt!

records.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते।
न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद् दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥
records.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśastasya vidyate
na hi kalyāṇakṛtkaścid durgatiṃ tāta gacchati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  He is not lost, thou Son of Pritha! No!
  Nor earth, nor heaven is forfeit, even for him,
  Because no heart that holds one right desire
  Treadeth the road of loss!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.40 The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, neither in this world, nor in the next world is there destruction for him; none, verily, who does good, O My son, ever comes to grief.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.40 Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or in the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.40 The Blessed Lord said O Partha, there is certainly no ruin for him here or hereafter. For, no one engaged in good meets with a deplorable end, My son!

records.sanskrit:
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः।
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥
records.iast:
prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃ lokānuṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo.abhijāyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He who should fail,
  Desiring righteousness, cometh at death
  Unto the Region of the Just; dwells there
  Measureless years, and being born anew,
  Beginneth life again in some fair home
  Amid the mild and happy.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.41 Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for everlasting years, he who fell from Yoga is rorn in a house of the pure and wealthy.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.41 Having reached the worlds where the righteous dwell, and having remained there for many years, he who has slipped from the path of spirituality will be born again in the family of the pure, benevolent and prosperous.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.41 Attaining the worlds of the righteous, and residing there for eternal years, the man fallen from Yoga is born in the house of the pious and the properous.

records.sanskrit:
अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम्।
एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥
records.iast:
athavā yogināmeva kule bhavati dhīmatām
etaddhi durlabhataraṃ loke janma yadīdṛśam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
It may chance
  He doth descend into a Yogin house
  On Virtue's breast; but that is rare! Such birth
  Is hard to be obtained on this earth, Chief!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.42 Or he is born in a family of even the wise Yogis; verily a birth like this is very difficult to obtain in this world.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.42 Or, he may be born in the family of the wise sages, though a birth like this is, indeed, very difficult to obtain.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.42 Or he is born in the family of wise yogis [Persons possessing knowledge of Brahman. (S. concedes that some rare householders also can have this knowledge, and he cites the instances of Vasistha, Agastya, Janaka and Asvapati of olden days, and Vacaspati and the author of Khanada of recent times.)] only. Such a birth as is of this kind is surely more difficult to get in the world.

records.sanskrit:
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम्।
यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
records.iast:
tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam
yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṃsiddhau kurunandana
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
So hath he back again what heights of heart
  He did achieve, and so he strives anew
  To perfectness, with better hope, dear Prince!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.43 Thee he comes in touch with the knowledge acired in his former body and strives more than before for perfection, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.43 Then the experience acquired in his former life will revive, and with its help he will strive for perfection more eagerly than before.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.43 There he becomes endowed with that wisdom acired in the previous body. and he strives more than before for perfection, O scion of the Kuru dynasty.

records.sanskrit:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः।
जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
records.iast:
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśo.api saḥ
jijñāsurapi yogasya śabdabrahmātivartate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
For by the old desire he is drawn on
  Unwittingly; and only to desire
  The purity of Yog is to pass
  Beyond the Sabdabrahm, the spoken Ved.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.44 By that very former practice he is borne on in spite of himself. Even he who merely wishes to know Yoga goes beyond the Brahmic word.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.44 Unconsciously he will return to the practices of his old life; so that he who tries to realise spiritual consciousness is certainly superior to one who only talks of it.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.44 For, by that very past practice, he is carried forward even in spite of himself! Even a seeker of Yoga transcends the result of the performance of Vedic rituals!

records.sanskrit:
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः।
अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
records.iast:
prayatnādyatamānastu yogī saṃśuddhakilbiṣaḥ
anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But, being Yogi, striving strong and long,
  Purged from transgressions, perfected by births
  Following on births, he plants his feet at last
  Upon the farther path.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.45 But the Yogi who strives with assiduity, purified of sins and perfected gradually through many births, reaches the highest goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.45 Then after many lives, the student of spirituality, who earnestly strives, and whose sins are absolved, attains perfection and reaches the Supreme.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.45 However, the yogi, applying himself assiduously, becoming purified from sin and attaining perfection through many births, thery acheives the highest Goal.

records.sanskrit:
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः।
कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥
records.iast:
tapasvibhyo.adhiko yogī jñānibhyo.api mato.adhikaḥ
karmibhyaścādhiko yogī tasmādyogī bhavārjuna
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Such as one ranks
  Above ascetics, higher than the wise,
  Beyond achievers of vast deeds! Be thou
  Yogi Arjuna!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.46 The Yogi is thought to be superior to the ascetics and even superior to men of knowledge (obtained through the study of scriptures); he is also superior to men of action; therefore be thou a Yogi, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.46 The wise man is superior to the ascetic and to the scholar and to the man of action; therefore be thou a wise man, O Arjuna!

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.46 A yogi is higher than men of austerity; he is considered higher even than men of knowledge. The yogi is also higher than men of action. Therefore, O Arjuna, do you become a yogi.

records.sanskrit:
योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना।
श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥
records.iast:
yogināmapi sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā
śraddhāvānbhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And of such believe,
  Truest and best is he who worships Me
  With inmost soul, stayed on My Mystery!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 6.47 And among all the Yogis he who, full of faith and with his inner self merged in Me, worships Me is deemed by Me to be the most devout.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 6.47 I look upon him as the best of mystics who, full of faith, worshippeth Me and abideth in Me."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 6.47 Even among all the yogis, he who adores Me with his mind fixed on Me and with faith,he is considered by Me to be the best of the yogis.
